claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can be homogenized into a high-temperature single-phase BCC state at or above 1000 °C.
Short-range ordering of Ni and Al within the BCC matrix drives a partial B2-type ordering transition during cooling and thermal exposure.
The proposed ordering transition produces a distinct B2 phase that competes or coexists with disordered BCC.
Competition or coexistence between B2 and disordered BCC explains the range of phases observed in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
The structural mediator is nanoscale Ni–Al short-range order that nucleates as B2 domains in a disordered BCC matrix.
Ni and Al have a local energetic preference for occupation of ordered sites in this alloy.
At intermediate temperatures, the energetic preference for Ni–Al ordering overcomes configurational entropy and causes B2 precipitation.
Prolonged aging at intermediate temperature permits diffusion-assisted formation of stable ordered precipitates.
Slower cooling permits sufficient Ni and Al diffusion to form stable B2 regions.
Rapid quenching suppresses large-scale B2 precipitation by limiting diffusion.
Slower cooling or longer aging will increase B2 phase fraction and precipitate size relative to a water-quenched, unaged baseline.
A sample water-quenched from above 1000 °C and left unaged will remain predominantly disordered BCC with negligible B2 features.
The ordering mechanism is relevant below about 900 °C for compositions near Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 because diffusivities permit local Ni–Al reorganization.
Above approximately 1000 °C, B2 dissolves into the high-temperature BCC matrix.
Cooling rates above 1000 K/s largely suppress formation of B2 domains.
Below approximately 500 °C, diffusion-limited kinetics impede B2 precipitation.
Secondary Cr-containing phases may also form in this alloy.
